data.title: Optex Systems Announces $1.22 Million Order for Laser Filter Units
data.description:
RICHARDSON, TX / ACCESS Newswire / September 18, 2026 / Optex Systems Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq:OPXS), a leading manufacturer of precision optical sighting systems for domestic and worldwide military and commercial applications, announced today it has been awarded a new contract for Laser Filter Units associated with various night vision goggle systems. The order value is $1.22 million with deliveries covering January 2027 through December 2027.

The Applied Optics Center, a Division of Optex Systems, Inc., is the leading provider of laser protection optics and optical devices that protect both the soldiers' eyes as well as their state-of-the-art visual augmentation devices. Bill Bates, GM of Applied Optics Center stated, "AOC continues to be in the lead role as a supplier of laser protection optics and optical assemblies to the U.S. military. All AOC employees take great pride in the quality and performance of our optics used for protecting our war fighters. We continue to add capabilities and equipment which will expand our portfolio of thin-film coatings and assemblies. New engineering expertise and equipment has recently been added as we return to the world of infrared optical components. These additions will further cement our role in the world of optics related to the U.S. military."

With this new order, the current Optex backlog is in excess of $28.3 million.

ABOUT OPTEX SYSTEMS

Optex, which was founded in 1987, is a Richardson, Texas based ISO 9001:2015 certified concern, which manufactures optical sighting systems and assemblies, primarily for Department of Defense (DOD) applications. Its products are installed on various types of U.S. military land vehicles, such as the Abrams and Bradley fighting vehicles, Light Armored and Armored Security Vehicles, and have been selected for installation on the Stryker family of vehicles. Optex also manufactures and delivers numerous periscope configurations, rifle and surveillance sights, and night vision optical assemblies. Optex delivers its products both directly to the military services and to prime contractors. For additional information, please visit the Company's website at www.optexsys.com.

data.title: France's CNP Assurances considers takeover of Coface, Bloomberg News reports
data.description:
French insurance group CNP Assurances is considering a potential takeover of Coface , Bloomberg News reported on Friday, citing people with knowledge of the matter.

CNP is working on an offer for the credit insurer, the report added.

Deliberations are at an early stage, and CNP could decide against proceeding with an offer, the report said, adding that other bidders could emerge.

CNP and Coface declined to comment on the report.

CNP, or Caisse Nationale de Prevoyance, is a leading personal insurer in France, with operations across Europe and Brazil, according to its website.

Coface provides trade credit insurance that protects companies against the risk of customer non-payment. It also offers business information services, debt collection, single-risk insurance, surety bonds and factoring.

data.title: Responsible Energy Provides Update on ESTCP AFFF Destruction Demonstration
data.description:
MAITLAND, ON, Sept. 18, 2026 /CNW/ -- Responsible Energy Corporation () ("Responsible Energy" or the "Company") provides an update regarding testing of its Free Radical Gasification ("FRG™") technology under the U.S. Department of War Environmental Security Technology Certification Program ("ESTCP") at the U.S. Army Engineer Research and Development Center ("ERDC") in Vicksburg, Mississippi being conducted by Tetra Tech, Inc. ().

On September 15, 2026, Tetra Tech, Inc. publicly disclosed that preliminary testing conducted in July 2026 demonstrated that Responsible Energy's FRG achieved greater than 99.9% destruction and removal efficiency ("DRE") of undiluted aqueous film-forming foam ("AFFF"). Formal ESTCP validation trials are being conducted from September 15 through September 17, 2026. The Company will provide further information when validated results are available.

Inclusion of FRG in ESTCP does not constitute endorsement of FRG or the Company by the United States government.

Responsible Energy Corporation is a Canadian clean technology company commercializing its patented Free Radical Gasification (FRG™) technology for the destruction of PFAS, AFFF and other hazardous liquid waste streams. data.title: What's Moving Markets Today? — WSJ
data.description:
By Shradha Dinesh

Major indexes edged lower as the yield on the 10-year Treasury note pushed past 5%.

Markets have had a lot to digest this week: a quarter-point interest-rate hike, fluctuating fuel prices and big tech's P(doom), aka the probability that AI results in a existentially catastrophic outcome, according to the Silicon Valley ecosystem.

Here's what is moving markets today:

Tech stocks: As bond yields climbed, driven by higher oil prices, tech stocks broadly flattened. Today's standouts are those behind AI infrastructure. Sandisk and Coherent posted 8% and 4% intraday gains, respectively.

Oil prices: Oil prices extended declines for a third consecutive session Friday on news that damage to Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and to an oil tanker hit in the Strait of Hormuz late on Thursday may not be as extensive as feared. Before prices reversed course, Brent crude recovered some of its losses after Bloomberg reported that Saudi Arabia told at least two European customers that they would not receive crude deliveries next month. Brent crude is just under $104 a barrel, or down 1%.

It's another big day for crypto and alternative assets: Bitcoin broke above $80,000. Strategy, Coinbase and MARA holdings are up more than 10%. Exchanges, like Robinhood and Bullish, and cryptocurrency miners are not far behind. The gains follow some new rules allowing exchanges to offer tokenized stocks and regulatory agencies stepping in to oversee crypto after the failure of a major bill this week.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: Volkswagen Warns on Profit After Big Porsche Write-Down — WSJ
data.description:
By Andrea Figueras and Mauro Orru

Volkswagen slashed its full-year profit forecast after flagging roughly $11.5 billion of impairment charges linked to its stake in Porsche, tough trading in China and its restructuring efforts.

The German carmaker said Friday that it now expected an operating return on sales of up to 1% this year, down from its prior estimate of between 4% and 5.5%. The new forecast, announced just before the market closed in Germany, sent Volkswagen shares down more than 5%.

The profit warning comes as Volkswagen contends with a range of challenges, including U.S. tariffs, rising manufacturing costs and increasingly fierce competition from Chinese automakers-in both China and Europe.

Earlier this month, Volkswagen's supervisory board approved a plan to double job cuts at the automaker to 100,000 and halve its model portfolio in a bid to remain competitive.

On Friday, the company said a further deterioration in market conditions-especially in China-as well as a shift in demand in favor of battery-electric vehicles would weigh on earnings, particularly at Audi and its Volkswagen brands.

Volkswagen said new assumptions about Porsche's prospects would result in a write-down of about 6 billion euros, the equivalent of about $6.89 billion. Volkswagen holds a stake of more than 75% in the sports-car brand.

Porsche has been contending with its own challenges, including a big bet on EVs that failed to pay off, U.S. tariffs and declining demand in China.

Volkswagen said it would take a further 2 billion euros in impairments in the second half of the year because of developments in the Chinese market and restructuring costs related to early-retirement programs and the planned sale of its Osnabrück factory in Germany.

The company said earlier this month that it was selling its Osnabrück plant to Israel's Aurelius Capital and the state of Lower Saxony, which aim to repurpose the site to make defense equipment.

In total, Volkswagen said, "special effects" amounting to 10 billion euros would weigh on operating profit this year, of which 900 million euros worth were already reported in the first half.

The company said revenue for the year is now expected to decline to about 315 billion euros from 321.9 billion euros in 2025, roughly in line with the midpoint of its previous guidance.

Volkswagen said its outlook was based on the assumption that tariffs would remain unchanged. It also noted that its estimates didn't take into account possible future effects from the war in the Middle East.

The company plans to publish its third-quarter report on Oct. 29.

data.title: This Little-Known Chip Stock Has Doubled. Wall Street Is Getting Bullish. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Ty Roush

MACOM Technology Solutions Holdings, a lesser-known semiconductor company benefiting from the accelerating data-center buildout, rose again Friday as Wall Street takes notice.

Shares of MACOM rose 4.7% and have surged 117% over the last year. The broader iShares Semiconductor ETF added 1%, while Broadcom advanced 2.2% and NXP Semiconductors N.V. fell 0.9%.

BMO Capital Markets upgraded MACOM to Outperform from Market Perform Thursday, even as its shares remain 33% below their all-time closing high of $409.68.

BMO is "excited" about MACOM's profit growth being driven by strong demand from artificial-intelligence data centers, while defense market "remains resilient," and that space is set to become a "material contributor" to growth in 2027, analyst Harsh Kumar wrote.

Kumar reiterated BMO's $335 price target for MACOM shares.

Wall Street has issued largely bullish views on MACOM shares in recent weeks, with 12 of the 16 firms polled by FactSet rating the stock a Buy.

Among them, Jefferies issued a price target of $450 for MACOM stock, about 71% above its Thursday closing price of $263.14, following the company's latest earnings in August.

Quarterly revenue rose 36% to $342.2 million-exceeding Wall Street estimates of $336 million, according to FactSet-as net income surged 176% to $100.7 million, MACOM reported last month.

MACOM announced a new suite of microchips Thursday designed to make optical communication inside AI data centers twice as fast as its earlier products. CEO Stephen Daly said the new chips would help deliver peak performance while cutting down on development efforts.

The announcement helped lift MACOM shares 4.5% Thursday, following a 4.8% increase on Wednesday.

data.title: Bitcoin Trades Above $80,000 to Clock Third Day of Gains — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Joseph Wilkins and Kirk Maltais

Bitcoin rose for a third consecutive day, topping the $80,000 level that has been a stubborn cap in recent weeks.

The move higher comes after Thursday's session saw a tech-fueled relief rally with broad gains seen from chip makers to data-storage companies across the major indexes. This uptick is being seen in both major cryptocurrencies and in stocks for companies involved with blockchain technology.

The flagship cryptocurrency rose 5.9% at $80,966, solidifying a course for a positive end to the week after it had slipped to a near four-week low on the U.S. Senate's rejection of the Clarity Act on Tuesday.

Gains were not limited to major cryptocurrencies, with Coinbase Global climbing 11%, Strategy Inc. rising 13% and Circle Internet Group up 7%.

The Federal Reserve's quarter-point interest-rate hike Wednesday has complicated the path for nonyielding assets such as bitcoin and gold, which tend to lose their relative shine in a rate-raising cycle when compared with the return offered by bonds.

The rate hike is one reason fund traders posted net outflows for bitcoin exchange-traded funds for six out of seven prior trading sessions. Flows changed course Thursday, posting a net inflow of $159.5 million into those ETFs on Thursday, according to data from CoinGlass.

Bitcoin could outperform gold in the coming months if investors unwind some of the short positions surrounding cryptocurrency ETFs, according to JPMorgan.

Analysts led by JPMorgan's Nikolaos Panigirtzoglou wrote that short interest in the flagship bitcoin ETF--iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF, or IBIT--remains close to year-to-date highs, while short interest in gold ETFs stands below historical averages.

"This contrast suggests that bitcoin still faces an overall more skeptical positioning backdrop than gold, perhaps due to more elevated hedging demand, despite the recent inflows and build up of futures positioning," the analysts wrote.

Analysts are eyeing targets above the $80,000 mark should bitcoin continue its upward momentum. In a note published Friday, analysts with Coinbase Research said resistance targets above $80,0000 are $83,000, then $90,000, and then $95,000.

Should the rally lose steam and see bitcoin retreating back below $70,000, prices are expected to keep falling back to yearly lows around $58,000, said Coinbase in its note.

Capital expenditures totaled $116,596 and the net profits calculation included a $62,500 net release from previously reserved funds.

  • Oil cash receipts for the period: approximately $1.25 million.
  • Natural gas cash receipts for the period: approximately $0.02 million.
  • Other revenue for the period: $0.11 million (includes salt water disposal income; reclassified from offset to lease operating expenses).
  • Total direct operating expenses (marketing, lease operating, workover): $0.66 million.

Business Highlights

  • Underlying natural gas sales volumes for the current month: 19,662 Mcf (634 Mcf/D), slightly lower than the prior month.
  • Average received wellhead prices: oil $79.81 per barrel (down from $88.13 prior month); natural gas $1.16 per Mcf (up from $0.64 prior month).
  • Severance and ad valorem taxes included in net profits: $0.06 million, modestly lower than the prior period.
  • Capital activity: $116,596 of capital expenditures reflecting tangible completion costs (including ~ $51,000 plugging costs and ~$63,000 workover costs), intangible completion costs, and a credit to tangible drilling costs; net release of reserved funds of $62,500 (release of $125,000 for workovers offset by a $62,500 ad valorem holdback).

At the time of writing, TSLA shares were trading 1% lower, heading for their first weekly fall in three weeks.

Barclays Sees Autonomous Driving Boost

Barclays analyst Dan Levy expects Tesla to deliver 475,000 vehicles in the third quarter (Q3), above the 466,000 estimate reportedly compiled by Bloomberg. This also beats Goldman Sachs’ estimates from earlier this week.

The firm maintained an ‘Equal Weight’ rating and $370 price target, according to The Fly. It represents a 2.2% upside from current levels.

Barclays said Tesla’s ramp-up of Full Self-Driving (FSD) supports the company’s broader autonomous-driving ambitions and could help improve margins. However, Levy said Tesla’s underlying fundamentals remain “mostly an afterthought” to its AI efforts.

FSD Could Find Favor In Europe, But Cybercab Faces Domestic Scrutiny

Tesla has increasingly positioned AI and autonomy at the center of its long-term growth story, spanning FSD, its Robotaxi network, and Optimus humanoid robots.

Tesla has continued to update its Full Self-Driving software, recently rolling out FSD v14.3.9. The carmaker is also pushing to expand FSD internationally, with Slovenia becoming the sixth European country to approve the system ahead of a potential broader EU rollout.

However, FSD still requires active driver supervision and does not make Tesla vehicles fully autonomous.

Meanwhile, its Cybercab is facing fresh regulatory scrutiny. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has reportedly asked Tesla to explain by September 30 how it certified the robotaxi, including whether temporary human-operated controls were used during the process.

Goldman Sachs Has A More Cautious View

Barclays’ delivery forecast contrasts sharply with Goldman Sachs, which cut its Q3 estimate to 435,000 vehicles from 490,000.

Goldman said sales in Tesla’s key U.S., Chinese and European markets were tracking below its earlier expectations, even if strength in Southeast Asia, South America and Australia could partly offset that weakness.

Tesla delivered 480,126 vehicles in the second quarter (Q2), rebounding sharply from 358,023 in Q1. Barclays’ estimate would represent only a slight sequential decline, while Goldman’s forecast implies a drop of about 9%.

Retail’s Take On TSLA

Retail sentiment for TSLA on Stocktwits remained ‘extremely bearish’ over the past 24 hours.

TSLA is down more than 17% so far in 2026, easily the worst-performing stock among the so-called Magnificent 7.

data.title: Expectation vs reality: Why you should not assume 20%+ equity returns-what Nifty 500 historical data reveals
data.description:
New Delhi, Sept. 18 -- When equity markets deliver strong returns, it can be easy for investors to start treating those gains as a new baseline. But history suggests that very high returns are not what investors experience most often.

In an X post, Niranjan Avasthi, President at Edelweiss Asset Management, highlighted the importance of keeping return expectations realistic. "When markets deliver unusually strong returns, it is tempting to treat those outcomes as the new normal," he noted.

Data reveals that across 258 three-year rolling return observations for the Nifty 500 TRI since 2005, the most common outcome was a CAGR of 10%-20%. This range accounted for 119 observations, or 46% of the total.

A three-year rolling return measures the annualised return earned over every possible three-year period within the data set, with the observation moving forward month by month.

For example, one observation would measure the annualised return from January 2005 to January 2008, the next from February 2005 to February 2008, and so on. This gives investors a much broader picture of the range of outcomes than simply looking at the Nifty 500's return over one fixed three-year period.

The data shows that a three-year CAGR between 10% and 20% was the most frequently observed outcome.

"Across 258 monthly observations of rolling 3-year CAGR returns since 2005 for the Nifty 500, the most common outcome was a return between 10% and 20%. This range occurred 119 times, i.e., 46% of all observations, making it the clearest centre of gravity in the data," Avasthi mentioned.

"The latest rolling three-year CAGR is 12.9%, broadly within this dominant band. This does not indicate weak performance; rather, it is consistent with the return experience investors have encountered most frequently," he added.

This does not mean investors will earn 10%-20% in every three-year period. Equity returns can vary sharply depending on when an investor enters and exits the market.

The data shows that strong three-year outcomes were relatively less frequent. "Higher-return periods do occur, but they should be viewed as a bonus rather than the baseline," he noted.

He added, "Returns between 20% and 30% appeared in 32 observations, or 12% of the sample. Returns above 30% occurred 41 times, representing 16%. These phases can materially accelerate wealth creation, but their relative rarity makes them unsuitable as permanent assumptions for financial plans or investor expectations."

At the other end, 13 observations, or 5%, recorded returns between -10% and 0%. Another 53 observations, or 21%, delivered returns between 0% and 10%. No three-year rolling period in the dataset recorded a CAGR below -10%.

Not necessarily.

"The historical average is 17.5%, while the median is 15.0%, reinforcing that mid-teen expectations are a more practical planning anchor than exceptional bull-market outcomes," he noted.

According to Avasthi, this suggests that investors may find mid-teen return expectations more practical for financial planning than assuming that exceptionally strong market returns will continue.

He summed up the point: "Equity investing rewards patience, but expectations matter. Investors who plan around sustainable mid-teen outcomes are less likely to be disappointed by normal market cycles or tempted to chase risk after unusually strong periods."

"Mid-teen returns are the planning anchor; exceptional returns are like bonus," he noted.
